title: HackNova 2026: 36-Hour National Hackathon
tagline: Build the autonomous future with AI & Cloud
description: A premier 36-hour national hackathon bringing together over 500 student developers to build disruptive AI, cloud, and web3 prototypes. Participants collaborate in teams to solve industry-sponsored problem statements under senior engineering mentorship.
fullDescription: HackNova 2026 is our premier 36-hour hackathon bringing together students to solve real-world problems. Participants will have 24/7 access to high-performance compute clusters, specialized IoT hardware kits, and continuous mentorship from senior engineers at leading tech firms. Tracks include Autonomous Agents, Generative Media, Decentralized Systems, and HealthTech.
organizer: Department of Computer Science & ACM Student Chapter

pdfDetails.detailedDescription:
HackNova 2026 is our premier 36-hour continuous software engineering hackathon designed to test algorithmic innovation, rapid prototype development, and technical resilience.
Participants will form multidisciplinary teams to tackle challenges in autonomous AI agents, distributed systems, generative media, and campus sustainability.
Teams have 24/7 access to high-performance GPU compute clusters and specialized hardware debugging benches provided by the school of computing.
Mentors from leading tech firms and open-source foundations will conduct continuous technical reviews and architecture consultations throughout the event.
Deliverables include a functional source repository, live demo deployment, and a 5-minute technical defense before the industry evaluation panel.
Prerequisites include basic proficiency in modern programming languages, version control with Git, and fundamental knowledge of APIs or web architectures.

schedule.activity: Opening Ceremony & Track Problem Statements Release

rules: Teams must consist of 2 to 4 members. Inter-college and inter-disciplinary teams are permitted.
All application code, assets, and design schemas must be created strictly during the hackathon timeline.
Third-party libraries, open-source frameworks, and public APIs are permitted provided they are disclosed in the README.
Pre-built closed proprietary software or prior commercial codebases are strictly prohibited and will result in disqualification.
Git commit history must clearly demonstrate incremental progress made during the designated hackathon hours.
Plagiarism or unauthorized copying of competing team intellectual property will lead to immediate expulsion.
Jury decisions on technical merit, innovation, and implementation rigor are final and binding.

title: Autonomous Drone & Robotics Bootcamp
tagline: Hands-on flight control, computer vision, and ROS2
description: A comprehensive engineering masterclass teaching drone aerodynamics, flight controller firmware calibration, optical flow vision stabilization, and autonomous waypoint navigation using ROS2.
fullDescription: Led by researchers and drone engineers, this intensive workshop covers quadcopter flight physics, PID controller tuning, optical flow sensor integration, and obstacle avoidance algorithms in Robot Operating System 2 (ROS2). Hardware kits provided for team sessions during the event.

pdfDetails.detailedDescription:
The Autonomous Drone & Robotics Bootcamp is a rigorous, practical masterclass bridging embedded systems, flight dynamics, and robotic vision.
Participants work in small engineering groups with modular quadcopter test kits, brushless ESC motors, and inertial measurement units (IMUs).
The curriculum spans airframe assembly, PID control tuning, telemetry transmission, and autonomous waypoint guidance using OpenCV and ROS2.
Faculty researchers and drone industry specialists guide students from initial motor spinning safety tests to indoor obstacle bypass demonstrations.
Attendees will master both hardware soldering/wiring protocols and software flight-stack configuration using open-source flight software.
Prerequisites include basic C++ or Python programming knowledge and an interest in robotics and mechatronics.

schedule.activity: Hardware Kit Distribution & Lab Safety Induction
Module 1: Quadcopter Dynamics & Brushless Motor Telemetry
Module 2: Flight Controller Assembly & Soldering Safety
Module 3: PID Tuning & Radio Transmitter Configuration
Module 4: Autonomous Waypoint Navigation & ROS2 Basics

rules: Laboratory safety goggles and enclosed footwear are mandatory inside the robotics testing area.
Quadcopter propellers must remain detached until authorized by a lab flight controller referee.
All drone flight tests must take place strictly inside the netted safety flight arena.
Components and telemetry equipment are property of the university lab and must be returned intact.
Participants must follow the instruction sequences provided by faculty supervisors.
Reckless handling of LiPo batteries or high-RPM motors will lead to immediate laboratory suspension.
Active participation throughout both hardware and software modules is required for certificate issuance.

Apex Venture is the premier student entrepreneurship and venture capital pitch competition on campus.
Founding teams pitch functional minimum viable products (MVPs), defensible market strategies, and financial projections before real angel investors.

title: Inter-Collegiate Futsal Derby
tagline: High-octane 5-a-side football under the floodlights
description: An adrenaline-fueled inter-collegiate 5-a-side futsal tournament played under international floodlights on the central turf complex, featuring 16 top university squads in knockout contention.
fullDescription: A fast-paced 5v5 futsal tournament held under floodlit astro-turf courts. Featuring group qualifiers leading into quarter, semi, and grand finals with licensed match officials. Teams will compete for championship trophies, medals, golden boot awards, and cash prizes.

pdfDetails.detailedDescription:
The Inter-Collegiate Futsal Derby is a premier 5-a-side football championship featuring high-paced technical play and tactical precision.
Sixteen selected university squads battle across group and knockout rounds on the campus floodlit artificial turf arena.
Matches are officiated by accredited state football referees following international FIFA futsal guidelines with rolling substitutions.
The tournament demands exceptional ball control, quick tactical transitions, sharp finishing, and collective team stamina.
Spectators experience stadium-style commentary, electronic scoreboards, and energetic campus derby rivalries.
Prerequisites include registered team rosters of certified college athletes possessing matching team kits and shin guards.

schedule.activity: Golden Boot, Best Goalkeeper & Trophy Presentation

rules: Teams comprise 5 on-field players (including 1 goalkeeper) and up to 3 rolling substitutes.
Matches consist of two 15-minute halves with a 3-minute half-time interval.
Standard futsal rules apply: no sliding tackles from behind, 4-second restart rule, and accumulated team fouls.
Players must wear protective shin guards and non-marking turf football shoes; metal studs are strictly prohibited.
Yellow and red card disciplinary policies will be strictly enforced by the match referee.
In the event of a tie in knockout rounds, matches proceed directly to a 3-kick penalty shootout.
The match referee's decision on on-field fouls and scoring is absolute and unquestionable.

pdfDetails.detailedDescription:
DefendTheNet 2026: Campus CTF Challenge is our premier campus technical event bringing together aspiring students across university departments.
The competition provides an accredited collegiate platform for participants to showcase technical expertise, creative ingenuity, and collaborative problem-solving.
Under the evaluation of faculty jurors and domain specialists, participants navigate carefully structured competitive rounds and practical challenges.
Attendees will test their applied abilities, benchmark their performance against peer institutions, and gain valuable industry-aligned feedback.
Key activities include structured qualification rounds, live competitive sessions, and formal evaluation defenses before the judging panel.
Prerequisites include Basic knowledge of algorithms, programming fundamentals, and system design.
rules: Participants must present a valid university student identity card at the reporting desk.
Individual and team participation must conform strictly to published track requirements.
All source code and technical submissions must be original work created during the competition.
Plagiarism or unauthorized copying of third-party intellectual property results in disqualification.
Use of permitted developer tools, IDEs, and standard libraries must be documented in submission files.
Submissions must be finalized before the announced deadline; late entries will not be evaluated.
The technical jury decisions on implementation rigor, efficiency, and originality are final.
